title: Five South Florida things to do this week
igCaption:
Start with the free and cheaper picks this week: James Turrell at Superblue, king tide parking help, and late-night Brightline trains after Kaseya Center shows.
Partners Pink Run is October 10, and Habibi Miami is marking two years on the Miami River.
Which one are you doing this week?

Sources: Miami New Times, Secret Miami, Florida Weekly, Haute Living, Wikipedia

#MiamiEvents #SouthFlorida #ThingsToDoMiami #MiamiGuide

scenes.text: Need something to do this week without paying for a ticket? Start with these five.

Number five: James Turrell’s “Blue Sea Sky” is at Superblue Miami on Northwest Twenty-Third Street. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, first come, first served. The room-sized work was created for the immersive art space.
scenes.caption: Number 5: James Turrell’s “Blue Sea Sky” is at Superblue Miami on NW 23rd St. Access requires a complimentary on-site reservation, first come, first served. The room-sized work was created for the immersive art space.

scenes.text: Number four: check Miami’s 2026 king tide guide before you park near the water. Secret Miami has the season dates, flood zones, and where to park for free.
scenes.caption: Number 4: check Miami’s 2026 king tide guide before you park near the water. Secret Miami has the season dates, flood zones, and where to park for free.

scenes.text: Number three: Brightline late-night trains are running after scheduled Kaseya Center concerts through the end of the year. This week has Don Omar on October fourth, Jonas Brothers on October fifth, and Camilo on October ninth. If you take Brightline, check NEAR to see who rode over too.

scenes.text: Number two: register for the Partners Pink Run on October tenth. Florida Weekly says registration is open now.
scenes.caption: Number 2: register for the Partners Pink Run on Oct. 10. Florida Weekly says registration is open now.

scenes.text: And number one: Habibi Miami is celebrating its second anniversary with a Marrakech Souk on the Miami River. The party marks two years since it opened.

scenes.text: Which one are you doing, and what should we cover next? And if one of those spots leaves you wondering who that person was you kept passing but never met, NEAR shows you the people who walked past you.
